nodes.n: Friday. A dining table longer than a cricket pitch. Twelve chairs, three butlers, and a chandelier that probably costs more than Sonpur.
At the head: Harsh Malhotra. On his right: Rajan Sethi, Kunal's father, steel baron. Between them: Meera, in pale blue, perfect and silent.

nodes.t: So this is the boy from the debut. Kunal tells me you carry drinks very well.

choice.t: "I carried them till Kunal pulled his hamstring."
Say nothing. Smile at your plate.

nodes.n: A tiny old woman in a white saree is wheeled in. She looks at you over gold spectacles like she's reading your bank statement.

nodes.t: Move, Kunal. I want to sit next to the one who looks hungry.
I'm Meera's Nani. Her mother's mother. I'm eighty-one and I say whatever I want. Eat.

nodes.n: Under the table, the old phone in your pocket buzzes.

msgs.t: STOP looking at me. Eat the paneer. It's the only good thing here.

choice.t: Text back: "The paneer is the second best thing here."
Text back: "This is dangerous. I'm stopping."
Put the phone away and talk to Nani.

nodes.n: Across the table Meera chokes on her water. Kunal pats her back. Nani looks from her face to yours, very slowly.

nodes.t: Do you know why they're all smiling, beta? Because my son-in-law owes Sethi three hundred crore, and my granddaughter is the repayment plan.
Her mother would have burned this house down. I'm too old to find the matches.
A toast. To the Monarchs, to the season, and to a date. My daughter will marry Kunal on the evening of the final. At the stadium. In front of everyone.

nodes.n: Applause. Glasses ring. Meera smiles at her father. Under the table, the old phone buzzes once.

nodes.cliff: One word. And the wedding is on the night of the final.
